A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DenseMarks work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised, relocated and removed content.

before.justification: V1 reports original correspondence measurements in Table 1, tracking and reconstruction demonstrations, and original ablation and consistency analyses in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original correspondence and tracking results and reports additional ablations, robustness tests, chair experiments, head-pose estimation and manually annotated cross-person matching results.

M1.justification: The central ViT/DPT embedder and canonical-cube pipeline remain. V2 adds a downstream DenseMarks-to-head-pose regressor using MobileNet or a fully connected layer (Appendix F), and adapts supervision to chair keypoints and object masks (Appendix E). These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: V2 retains CelebV-HQ and Nersemble coverage while adding ShapeNet chair correspondence experiments, head-pose estimation on 300W-LP and AFLW2000-3D, and LPFF evaluations of cross-person matching, synthetic perturbations and challenging appearances. These substantially broaden object domains, tasks and tested input conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CSE and FaRL. CSE also enters Figure 3 and replaces Fit3D in Figure 5, although Fit3D remains in Table 1. New comparisons include PRNet in Table 12 and RGB-based pose regressors in Table 10. The fine-tuned DINOv3 comparator corresponds to the earlier no-canonical-space ablation, rather than an entirely new comparator.

E3.justification: V2 introduces same-person PCK@0.05 and cross-person PCK@0.1, the latter evaluated on 400 LPFF pairs from 30 manually annotated subjects. New protocols include half-budget training for Table 3 and Appendix B, a 90/10 training-validation split for pose regression, and synthetic perturbations of 300 LPFF images. The original main training schedule remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds loss-weight, smoothing, grid-resolution, tracker-confidence and tracker-choice ablations; corrupted-track, landmark and mask tests; synthetic image stress tests; failure cases; and a manual track-quality audit. The canonical-space ablation is retained and expanded. V1's pretraining ablation, ear-surface pose analysis and extended stereo-configuration analysis are removed.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, Appendix G specifies eight perturbation realizations per image and fits a Gaussian to correspondence-location estimates, reporting empirical standard deviation and entropy in Table 11. This adds variability estimation for one analysis, rather than uncertainty across training seeds or confidence intervals for the main benchmarks.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores remain, including DenseMarks MAE 3.68 and RMSE 5.90. V2 adds extensive results: Table 10 reports AFLW2000-3D MAE 5.97 degrees with DenseMarks versus 18.22 with RGB using MobileNet. Table 12 gives DenseMarks higher cross-person PCK than PRNet (0.85 versus 0.76), but PRNet better ArcFace and Met3R scores. Pretraining-ablation and extended stereo results disappear. New half-budget ablation scores do not establish same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the contrastive expression from norm(Feat1) multiplied by its own transpose to norm(Feat1) multiplied by norm(Feat2)'s transpose. This repairs the mathematical expression to match the cross-image objective already described in v1; it does not establish a new training algorithm. No theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal claims: compact, interpretable canonical embeddings, correspondence consistency across subjects and views, whole-head coverage, and benefits for matching and tracking. Additional experiments do not revise these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning interview-style training data, backside views, rapid motion, long hair and accessories. It interprets supervision-noise sensitivity and design tradeoffs, and discusses why PRNet can score better on face-focused ArcFace/Met3R measures while losing on PCK. V1's interpretation of volumetrically ordered ear surfaces is removed.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies grid resolution 128, Gaussian smoothing strength 1.5, the default tracker-confidence threshold 0.6, memory requirements, and preprocessing/training details for the new applications. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original settings. Conversely, v1 Appendix A.3's DLT reconstruction, downsampling, consistency tolerances and reprojection-threshold instructions are removed. The promised future code/checkpoint release remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting the new experiments, including ShapeNet, KeypointNet, LPFF, AllTracker and head-pose research, and discusses comparison with face-only PRNet in Appendix I. The main related-work organization and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged. Duplicate CSE and FaRL bibliography entries do not represent additional distinct works.

P1.justification: The original main narrative is largely retained. V2 consolidates baseline descriptions, brings canonical-space analysis into the main results, reorganizes the appendices, and adds explanatory and limitations paragraphs. Publication headers, acknowledgments and an LLM-use disclosure also change; the revision is not an extensive rewrite of the retained prose.

P2.justification: V2 expands and groups Table 1, revises comparator panels in Figures 3 and 5, reformats the canonical-space comparison, and adds numerous ablation, application and robustness displays. It removes pretraining, ear-surface and extended stereo panels. The lighting illustration is retained and relocated from Figure 12 to Figure 14. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central correspondence and robustness claims through relevant additional baselines, manually annotated cross-person PCK evaluation, and controlled supervision-noise and design studies. Explicit failure cases and limitations also clarify applicability. These address v1's reliance on proxy cross-person metrics and mostly qualitative robustness evidence. The gains outweigh the loss of the pretraining analysis and detailed stereo-reconstruction instructions, despite unchanged headline benchmark scores.
